seo.title: OMP vs HagiCode: Features and Comparison
seo.description: omp (oh-my-pi) is a free, MIT-licensed terminal coding agent; HagiCode is a workbench that runs it. Compare features, pricing and fit.

summary: omp, short for oh-my-pi, is an MIT-licensed terminal coding agent forked from Pi, with LSP, debugger and browser tools built in. HagiCode is a desktop and web workbench that runs omp as its executor, so the two work together rather than compete.

content: omp is oh-my-pi, a terminal coding agent you install and run from the command line. It started as a fork of Pi and adds IDE-style tooling such as LSP, a debugger, subagents and a browser. HagiCode is a different layer: a desktop and web workbench that launches agent CLIs, including omp, and gives you sessions, specs, commits and history around them. It does not replace omp, and it does not host models.

If you work alone in a terminal, run omp interactively or in scripts, and are happy tracking your own tasks, stay with omp. Add HagiCode when you want several omp tasks running in parallel, with a written proposal and a reviewable history for each one.

sections.title: omp vs HagiCode at a glance

cells: What it is
Terminal coding agent, a fork of Pi, with LSP, debugger, browser and subagent tools built in
AI programming workbench that runs agent CLIs (including omp) as executors
Interface and platforms
Terminal UI, one-shot print mode, RPC, SDK, ACP for editors; macOS, Linux, Windows
Desktop app (Windows, macOS, Linux), Docker Compose container, Microsoft Store edition
Pricing and licensing
MIT-licensed and free; you pay only for the models you connect
Desktop and Container editions free; Store edition free base, optional one-time TurboEngine purchase
Model and provider access
Many providers (README says 60+), custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints, per-role model routing
Hosts no models; uses omp's own sign-in, or OmniRoute routing if you configure it
Parallel work
Subagents run in isolated worktrees inside one session
Several sessions side by side, managed as named Agents
Spec and planning workflow
Planning model role and a review command; proposal tracking is up to you
OpenSpec proposals: propose, validate, apply, archive
Git and commit handling
Built-in omp commit splits changes into atomic commits
AI-written commit messages with repository locking; Git management in the UI
Asking you questions
Built-in structured questions in its terminal UI
Shows omp's questions in the conversation, then continues the same run
Setup effort
One install command, then sign in or add an API key
Install omp first, then HagiCode, then pick OMP as the Agent CLI
Best for
Terminal-first developers who want deep tooling and scripting
Running several omp tasks across repos with specs, review and history in one place

items.title: IDE-grade tooling inside the terminal
content: The README lists 14 LSP operations and 28 DAP operations. File renames go through the language server, so imports update before a file moves. Debugger sessions work with lldb-dap, dlv and debugpy.
It also keeps persistent Python and Bun workers that can call the agent's own tools, and drives Chromium tabs for browser work.

items.title: Edits that fail safe
content: Hashline edits anchor each change to a content hash and are rejected if the file has moved on. ast_edit previews a structural change before it is applied.
Stream rules let a regex match abort the stream and inject a rule before the model retries, which is useful for keeping a model on your conventions.

items.title: Subagents and model roles
content: The task tool fans work out to subagents in isolated worktrees and returns schema-validated results. An advisor role lets a second model review each turn.
Models are routed by role (default, smol, slow, plan, commit, vision, task, advisor, tiny), with fallback chains and path-scoped model sets configured in ~/.omp/agent/config.yml.

items.title: Many ways in, and your existing rules come along
content: You can run it as a terminal UI, a one-shot omp -p command, an RPC process over stdio, a Node SDK, or an ACP server for editors such as Zed.
It reads rules and MCP servers from .claude, .cursor, .codex, .cline and other tool folders, so moving to omp does not mean rewriting your project instructions.

sections.title: When to choose omp, and when to choose HagiCode

items: Choose omp alone if you work in a terminal and want LSP, debugger and browser tools without a GUI.
Choose omp alone if you run it in scripts or CI with omp -p, where a workbench adds nothing.
Choose omp alone if you already track tasks in your own issue tracker and do not want a proposal step.
Choose omp alone if your work is mostly one repository and one task at a time.
Choose HagiCode if you want several omp sessions running at once, each with its own context and status.
Choose HagiCode if you want every change to start from a written proposal and end with an archived record.
Choose HagiCode if one feature spans several repositories and you want them declared once instead of explained each time.
Choose HagiCode if you prefer a graphical view of sessions, tool calls and diffs to a terminal scrollback.
Choose HagiCode if you switch between agents and want one interface for omp, Claude Code, Codex and others.

blocks.title: Where HagiCode is not the right tool for omp work
content: Headless CI and scripted one-shot runs: call omp -p directly. HagiCode is built around interactive sessions.
Terminal-only habits: if you do not want a GUI, HagiCode only adds a layer between you and omp.

Features that live in omp's own terminal UI, such as slash commands or /collab sharing, should not be assumed to appear in HagiCode. HagiCode runs omp in print mode, or in rpc-ui mode when a run may ask questions.

It needs omp installed and signed in first, so setup is longer than running omp alone. The free editions allow 3 concurrent proposals, and the embedded Code Server is not a replacement for a full IDE.

HagiCode does not bundle or replace omp. It looks for the omp executable on your machine, checks its version, and starts it for each run, so your omp install, sign-in and configuration stay exactly as they are.
HagiCode passes the working directory and the model you chose, and can set omp's provider, thinking level, no-session mode and tool restrictions from its settings.

items: Install omp (for example curl -fsSL https://omp.sh/install | sh) and sign in or add an API key for your provider.
Install HagiCode Desktop for Windows, macOS or Linux.
In HagiCode, choose OMP as the Agent CLI and pick a model; if you use OmniRoute, select it as the route.
Open a repository and start a session or a proposal.
Expect the run to stream into the conversation, with tool calls shown in the shared tool-call view.
To go back, run omp in your terminal as before. Nothing in your omp setup or your repository is locked to HagiCode.

blocks.title: What works with omp inside HagiCode
content: Works: parallel sessions, proposals, AI commits, the tool-call view, version detection and health checks, and interactive questions (omp's structured questions appear in the conversation).
Does not apply: the agent work panel is Claude-only, and omp's terminal-UI-only features are not surfaced.

sections.title: What HagiCode adds on top of any agent

items.title: Parallel sessions and Agents management
content: Each omp run in HagiCode is its own session, so you can have one working on the API while another writes tests. Agents management gives every session a name and a visible status instead of a row of terminal tabs.

items.title: OpenSpec proposals
content: A task starts as a proposal and moves through propose, validate, apply and archive. The reasoning behind an omp change stays next to the diff. Free editions allow 3 concurrent proposals.

items.title: AI commit and Code Server
content: HagiCode writes the commit message from your diff and locks the repository while it commits. The embedded Code Server opens the file omp changed in a browser editor. omp's own commit command still works in a terminal.

items.title: Monospecs and Vault
content: Monospecs declares your repositories in one file so omp starts a proposal with the full change surface. Vault stores reference projects and notes that new proposals can use as context.

items.title: OmniRoute, tool-call view and TokenMonitor
content: If you configure OmniRoute, omp's model requests can be routed through it. Tool calls from omp are shown in the same format as other agents. An optional status-bar item shows today's tokens and cost from TokenMonitor, off by default.

items.title: Interactive questions
content: When omp asks a structured question, HagiCode shows it in the conversation, the session waits for a reply, and your answer continues the same run. If the run already ended, the answer goes in as a normal message in the same session.
bullets: Questions asked at the same time can be answered in one submission;
A question unanswered after 30 minutes expires and can still be answered by a follow-up message;
Enabled per CLI by the interactive-control setting.

items: omp is a capable, free, MIT-licensed terminal agent; HagiCode is a workbench that runs it and does not replace it.
Stay with omp alone for terminal-first, single-task, scripted or CI work.
Add HagiCode for parallel sessions, proposals, commit assistance and multi-repo context around the same omp install.
Trying both costs little: your omp setup is untouched, and you can return to the terminal at any time.

faq.question: Is omp free?
faq.answer: omp is MIT-licensed and free to install. You pay for the models you connect, either with API keys or, for some providers, an existing subscription you sign in to. See omp.sh for current details.

faq.question: How do I install omp?
faq.answer: On macOS or Linux run curl -fsSL https://omp.sh/install | sh. On Windows run irm https://omp.sh/install.ps1 | iex. Homebrew (brew install can1357/tap/omp) and Bun (bun install -g @oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent) also work.

faq.question: Is omp the same as Pi?
faq.answer: No. omp is a fork of Pi that was rewritten as a coding-first tool with many more built-in tools. Pi stays minimal and leaves features like subagents to extensions.

faq.question: Can I use omp with HagiCode?
faq.answer: Yes. HagiCode lists OMP as an Agent CLI. Install and sign in to omp, then select it in HagiCode; it runs omp for you and keeps your omp setup unchanged.

faq.question: Does HagiCode replace omp?
faq.answer: No. HagiCode is the workbench around omp, adding sessions, proposals, commits and history. It needs omp installed and signed in to run.

faq.question: omp vs HagiCode: which should I pick?
faq.answer: Pick omp alone if you work in a terminal on one task at a time or in scripts. Add HagiCode if you want parallel sessions, proposals and a visual history around omp.
